design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (hardware_procurement_orders), revision 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,5,4]; cancellation fee 4, staged revision 5, approval deposit 4.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only for her four ordered laptops to 'come set up and enrolled with Autopilot instead of plain, still on rush'. The approval-deposit rule waits on 'that staged quote carries a quote date no earlier than the cancellation date of the line it takes over' (HQ-052419 is dated 2026-09-24) and the revision rule waits on 'the order it re-quotes shows status cancelled and its ledger carries the cancellation fee charged on it' (HQ-052418 is ordered with an empty ledger), so the agent must discover cancellation -> revision -> approval and compute three multi-factor figures over ClearPath (managed) and Microsoft 365 (licensing) records.
SCOPE: task 0 claims the endpoint schedules (hardware_ext_endpoint_cancellation_fee, hardware_ext_staged_requote_total, hardware_ext_endpoint_approval_deposit; tools sign_order_cancellation_55862425, revise_staged_quote_eb003c71, sign_quote_approval_0590c0d2). Task 1 claims the infrastructure schedules (Network/Server cancellation fee, the deposit credit of a cancelled infrastructure order, the re-issue of a lapsed infrastructure quote and the Network/Server approval deposit); the two scopes share no policy or tool.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root = approval deposit (user). Edge 1 approval -> revision: value_input, gate b_quote_total, state form ('is not fixed until'); false at frozen_time: initial_state.hardware_orders.a7854dfb-ef00-4749-a032-4be5a509e75d.quote_date = 2026-09-24 and the plain order is not cancelled; only revise_staged_quote_eb003c71 re-dates a staged endpoint quote. Edge 2 revision -> cancellation: value_input, gate b_cancel_fee, state form ('only after'); false: initial_state.hardware_orders.f1a9b68c-b331-49e8-b5f7-46fe9aaa4032.status = ordered with no fee row; only sign_order_cancellation_55862425 (user) books an endpoint cancellation fee. Order: cancellation (14), revision (16), approval (18), a chain. Deletion: no cancellation -> revision 5180.40 instead of 5080.40; no revision -> deposit 1667.83 instead of 1258.06.
FACTOR CARD - cancellation fee 543.07 (all-baseline 493.84): po_age_build method, PO 9 days -> percentage + 12.00/unit return freight (baseline 495.07); tier_fee_rate Professional 8 (baseline 10%: 641.84); expedite_forfeit rush quoted, quote approved 9 days before -> 75.00 (baseline 0: 468.07); arrears_admin_charge one late fee in 12 months -> 25.00 (baseline 0: 518.07; near-miss 2025-10-01 late fee exactly 12 months old).
FACTOR CARD - staged revision 5080.40 (all-baseline 5453.40): autopilot_staging_rate multi-source (Premium or E3 plan AND active ClearPath) 55 (baseline 95: 5240.40); tenure_handling 30 months 15 (baseline 25: 5090.40); tier_rush_rate Professional 75 (baseline 150: 5155.40); fee_credit_basis method, same day, one late fee in 12 months -> lesser of 543.07 and 100.00 (baseline none: 5180.40); defender_onboarding_rate Premium or E3 plan, no E5 plan -> 8/unit (baseline 15: 5108.40).
FACTOR CARD - approval deposit 1258.06 (all-baseline 25% x 5080.40 = 1270.10): tier_deposit_share 20 (1499.98); arrears_deposit_points +5 (1016.14); managed_spend_relief 2689.45 >= half of 5080.40 -> -4 (1451.60); tenure_deposit_build method, 30 < 36 months -> service charges 242.00 + 21% of 4838.40 (1066.88).
NEAR-MISS CARD (revision 3): the staged revision's Defender onboarding tier — an expired Microsoft 365 E5 (no Teams) pilot (2 licences, P1Y annual, 54.75 x 12 x 2 = 1314.00 invoiced 2024-06-03 and paid, auto-renew off, licences removed at expiry 2025-06-03) would give the E5 tier (0 per unit, total 5048.40) if counted; the rule reads only active subscriptions (5080.40). The cancellation fee and deposit keep the 2025-10-01 ClearPath late fee (exactly 12 whole months old) as their near-miss.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: cancellation - hardware_cancellation.cancellable_stage (after PO, before shipment, cancellable_after_po true for Standard Endpoint): ordered, PO 2026-09-28, no ship date; verified_contact at step 1 (phone + PIN). Revision - hardware_quote_and_pricing / hardware_agg_multi_holding policy_scope. Approval - approve_in_validity: day 0 after the revision (day 13 on the original date); credit exposure 0 + 5080.40 <= 50000 (active ClearPath); verified_contact.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: plain order f1a9b68c-b331-49e8-b5f7-46fe9aaa4032 (HQ-052418, 4 x LAT5450-U5135U-16-512) supplies unit price 1209.60, rush and the fee; staged quote a7854dfb-ef00-4749-a032-4be5a509e75d (HQ-052419) is revised and approved; the closed monitor order 5485bf43-a213-4b8f-9c4e-acc387e46e51 with its paid final invoice is excluded. ClearPath: the client's single agreement 9a9dddbf-1d3b-40cb-9784-d3e45ad4e467 (go-live 2024-03-11 on ClearPath Essentials, signed tier change to ClearPath Professional effective 2025-02-01, request in managed_service_requests).
SEED ROWS (complete ledgers, priced by their charters): ClearPath agreement (36-month term 2024-03-11..2027-03-10, 19 contracted = covered seats, onboarding fee waived for a 36-month term), go-live baseline seat change of 19, baseline proration 1099.70 (85.44 x 19 x 21/31) on the first invoice, every monthly fee from 2024-04 (Essentials 89.00 less 4% = 85.44 x 19 = 1623.36) and from 2025-02 (Professional 149.00 less 5% = 141.55 x 19 = 2689.45), every fee priced as of its own posting day under the published current-month seat-pricing schedule: 2689.45 for 2025-02 and 2025-03 (posted before the Business Premium purchase of 2025-03-03), then 2689.45 less the 1.5% CSP licensing credit (19 active Business Premium licences against 19 seats; no Sentinel, Continuum, F3 or servers, fewer than 40 seats) = 2649.11 for every fee from 2025-04 to 2026-10, each paid on day 20 except the 2025-08 and 2026-04 fees; the 2026-10 fee (INV-310217, 2649.11) is open and equal to the agreement balance. Late fees under the published late-fee schedule (each was the only unpaid invoice; balance band 1000 at the rate + the rest at half rate; 25% recent-payment courtesy; no relationship courtesy): 2025-10-01 on INV-310119 at 1.0% (no late fee in 12 months, 11 payments), on the 2649.11 balance (10.00 + 8.24555) x 0.75 = 13.68 (above the 10.00 tenure minimum), paid with the August fee 2662.79 on 2025-10-08; 2026-06-01 on INV-310175 at 1.5% (the 2025-10-01 fee in the window), (15.00 + 12.368325) x 0.75 = 20.53 (minimum 5.00), paid with the April fee 2669.64 on 2026-06-10. Microsoft 365: the expired E5 pilot above, and Business Premium P1Y annual c450a5c5-bca5-4a95-95c3-d94cdbaf151b: signed order form, initial purchase of 19 licences, annual cycle charges 22.00 x 12 x 19 = 5016.00 on 2025-03-03 and 2026-03-03, both paid; no administration fee (both ClearPath tiers include M365 administration). Hardware: plain order X, staged quote Y, monitor order with its final invoice and payment, signed approval requests of X and the monitor order.
PERSONA: Renata Quillen, brisk office manager; volunteers only the set-up/Autopilot/rush wish and willingness to sign; gives phone then PIN when asked, HQ-052418 when asked, her other services only when asked; signs what is handed over, accepts stated amounts, ends when told the set-up order is approved.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate (name), verify (phone + PIN), read hardware orders, ledger and requests, the ClearPath agreement, its tier-change request, seat ledger and billing, the Microsoft 365 subscription, its order form, licence ledger and billing; hand over the cancellation (543.07); revise HQ-052419 (5080.40); hand over the approval (1258.06).

user_scenario: You are Renata Quillen, office manager at Thornbury Survey & Engineering, PLLC in Richmond, and the firm's authorized contact with Stratton Bay. You are calling on a busy Wednesday morning, friendly but brisk, about the four Dell Latitude laptops you ordered at the end of September for the new field engineers. They have not shipped yet. Your IT lead has now asked for them to arrive imaged and already enrolled through Autopilot, ready to hand out, instead of as plain laptops, and you want the rush kept because the engineers start soon. What you say at the start is simply this: "We'd like the four laptops we ordered to come set up and enrolled with Autopilot instead of plain, still on rush. If you can sort it out today I'll sign whatever needs signing." You expect the service desk to work out how that is done; you have no idea how their orders or fees work and you never suggest any step yourself. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your name and the registered phone number 9195550512, and when asked for a second detail you give the support PIN 538146; only if a third detail is requested do you add the EIN last four 5274. If asked which order, you say it is quote HQ-052418, the four Dell Latitude 5450 laptops. If asked about the firm's other services, you know you are on a ClearPath managed services agreement (moved up to the Professional tier early last year) and Microsoft 365 Business Premium, and you are happy for the agent to look those up. You do not know what anything will cost and you never quote a figure. When the agent explains that something has to be signed by you, you agree and, as soon as the agent hands it to you, you sign it yourself. If the agent tells you a charge or a deposit, you accept it as long as it is what their schedule says; you do not argue the amount and you never propose a different one. If the agent mentions a configuration sheet or anything your IT lead has to send later, you say your IT lead Tomas will take care of it. Once the agent tells you the set-up laptop order is approved, you thank them and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the client profile the caller names and read its client reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed by the client reference number; without it no order, agreement or subscription can be found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's hardware orders: the four-laptop Standard Endpoint Order HQ-052418 (ordered, quote approved and purchase order placed 2026-09-28, rush, unit price 1209.60, total 4938.40), the Staged Endpoint quote HQ-052419 for the same four laptops (quoted 2026-09-24, total 5393.40) and the closed monitor order that is not concerned.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The staged quote is the one the client can sign for set-up laptops; its revision is priced only once the plain order shows cancelled with its fee, and its deposit only once it carries a quote date no earlier than that cancellation (the two prerequisite sentences), so the agent must see that the plain order is still ordered and the staged quote is still dated 2026-09-24. Purchase order date, quantity, unit price, quote total and rush flag feed the fee, the revision and the deposit.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's hardware ledger: the closed monitor order's final invoice and payment, and no entry at all for the laptop order HQ-052418.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: 'A re-quote of a cancelled endpoint line is priced only after the order it re-quotes shows status cancelled and its ledger carries the cancellation fee charged on it.' — the laptop order's ledger has no cancellation fee yet; the monitor order's rows are settled and concern nothing here.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's hardware requests: the signed approvals of HQ-052418 and of the closed monitor order, and no cancellation request for the laptop order.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that no cancellation of the plain laptop order has been registered or signed, so the order stays live until the client signs one in this call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's single ClearPath agreement: ClearPath Professional (tier change effective 2025-02-01), go-live 2024-03-11, 19 seats at 141.55.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The ClearPath tier sets the fee percentage, the rush charge and the deposit share; the agreement being active sets the staging tier, and its Microsoft 365 tenant-administration coverage the security preparation tier; the go-live date sets the handling charge and the deposit build; seat rate times seats sets the managed-spend relief.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the signed tier-change request from ClearPath Essentials to ClearPath Professional, effective 2025-02-01.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that the Professional tier is a tier change on the agreement that went live 2024-03-11, so the tenure runs from that go-live date.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the agreement's seat ledger: the go-live baseline of 19 seats and no later change.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms the 19 covered seats the managed-spend relief multiplies by the seat rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the ClearPath billing ledger: every monthly fee and payment since go-live and the late fees of 2025-10-01 and 2026-06-01.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the 2026-06-01 late fee is fewer than twelve whole months old; that count sets the administration charge of the cancellation and the late-payment points of the deposit, and, being one rather than none, keeps the staged re-quote off the whole-fee credit.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Microsoft 365 subscriptions: the active Microsoft 365 Business Premium subscription and the Microsoft 365 E5 (no Teams) pilot subscription that expired on 2025-06-02.

edges.condition: The quoted Staged Endpoint Order for the same part number and quantity has a quote_date on or after the cancelled_date of the Standard Endpoint Order whose line it takes over, carrying the revised quote_total_usd.
edges.policy_source: The deposit on a staged quote that takes over a plain endpoint line cancelled after its purchase order is not fixed until that staged quote carries a quote date no earlier than the cancellation date of the line it takes over.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The staged quote is still dated 2026-09-24 with its base total 5393.40, and the plain line it would take over is not even cancelled yet.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The revision re-dates HQ-052419 to 2026-10-07 (the cancellation day) and replaces its total with 5080.40, which the deposit is built on.

edges.condition: The Standard Endpoint Order being re-quoted has status cancelled with cancellation_stage after_po, and its hardware billing ledger carries one hardware_cancellation_fee entry.
edges.policy_source: A re-quote of a cancelled endpoint line is priced only after the order it re-quotes shows status cancelled and its ledger carries the cancellation fee charged on it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The laptop order is still live (ordered, purchase order placed 2026-09-28, not shipped) and its billing ledger has no entry at all.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The signed cancellation sets the order to cancelled (after_po, cancelled 2026-10-07) and books the 543.07 cancellation fee, so b_cancel_fee = 543.07 and the credit basis deducts 100.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (approval <- re-quote <- cancellation): each problem has one prerequisite, so the only topological order is cancellation, re-quote, approval; no parallel prerequisites exist to reorder.
